questions.q: What is a SQL Server Database Project (.sqlproj)?
options: A single giant .sql file containing the entire schema
A proprietary binary format that can't be viewed as text
A structured, buildable collection of files representing a database schema, part of SQL Server Data Tools
A cloud-only Azure resource with no local file representation
questions.explain: .sqlproj organizes each object into its own file inside a structured project that SSDT can build and validate.

questions.q: What does 'building' a database project actually check?
options: That every stored procedure runs in under one second
That the database has enough disk space allocated
That all table names are in alphabetical order
That the schema is internally consistent — e.g. no view references a nonexistent column, no foreign key points at an undefined table
questions.explain: The build step parses and validates every script in the project, catching broken references before deployment.

questions.q: What does a schema comparison tool like SSDT's Schema Compare do?
options: Automatically merges two databases into one without review
Only works when comparing two live SQL Server instances, never a project file
Deletes any objects that exist in only one of the two schemas being compared
Diffs two schemas (e.g. a project and a live server) and can generate a script to reconcile the differences
questions.explain: Schema Compare produces an itemized diff between a source and target schema, plus an optional script to bring them in line.

options: The difference between two branches in Git before they're merged
A SQL Server feature that automatically renames columns
The gap between what source control says a schema should be and what a live database actually contains
The natural slowdown of query performance over time
questions.explain: Drift happens when a live database diverges from the reviewed, versioned definition — often from an out-of-process change.

questions.q: Where can you find schema comparison functionality, per this lesson?
options: It requires a third-party paid product with no Microsoft equivalent
SSDT's Schema Compare feature, and a comparable extension in Azure Data Studio
Only inside SQL Server Management Studio, nowhere else
It's a command only available through raw T-SQL, with no tooling
questions.explain: Both SSDT (Visual Studio) and Azure Data Studio provide schema comparison tooling for exactly this task.
